content:
﻿# 做了120个 side hustles，他现在月入$1万+

## 冷启动：8岁就开始编程

Mubs been indie hacking before had name and community。

Parents brought computer for older siblings when he was eight。

Got bored of two or three games came with it。

They stopped using。

He started coding。

Bought computer magazines and copied coding examples into computer。

Then modified program to do what wanted。

That's how learned to code。

Fell in love with it。

Even after going to university for computer science and coding for living for decades。

Still loves it。

Love to build things for himself。

That love turned into side hustles — LOT of side hustles — and indie hacking。

Until beginning of this year。

Most indie hacking done on weekends or evenings。

While working at fintech startup where been for four years。

Wanted more flexibility and autonomy during day。

Being full-time founder seemed best way to achieve。

Timing never quite right。

Until this year。

Now doing it full time。

Little more stressful than anticipated。

Really is something else have to make ALL decisions about everything every day。

## 反直觉：只花2-4周做项目，做不完就 kill

Recently hit 120 projects，total。

Took over 20 years。

Won't list all here，but can find all here。

Still holds record for most launches on Product Hunt — 85 of them。

Most successful was probably Will Robots Take My Job?

Got covered by magazines、newspapers、TV、radio all over world。

Did about 14M page views before sold。

Made about $4K/mo in ads at peak。

Most projects built because of problem personally experiencing。

In some cases，using existing piece of software doesn't work exactly how wants。

So builds solution for self。

Sometimes，finds there isn't market，outside of self。

But more often than not，finds many other people in same situation。

Might sound little crazy，building products when not sure if market。

In some cases，when knows isn't。

But limits time to work on each project to between two and four weeks。

If hasn't launched by then，spent too much time on it。

Likely，wouldn't finish after that point anyway。

So kills it。

Since able to build pretty quickly。

Worth scratching itch and building idea。

Even if doesn't amount to anything。

## 暴击：验证 MVP，不是验证想法

Validating before build doesn't work。

Lot of indie hackers recommend validating with landing page or some such before building anything。

But thinks much easier to validate once have working product。

Not finished product，but working product。

Just very very difficult to get good/accurate feedback on idea。

Even with sketch or mockup。

Potential users rarely truly understand what planning to build。

Having functioning MVP makes much more likely potential users able to give useful feedback。

Heck if like idea，can start using — and paying — right away。

##  punchline：前50个视频都是练习

Here's advice：

Make authentic content and stick with it。

Most people quit way too early。

First 50 videos，first 100 posts，first year of newsletter。

Almost none will look like working。

But authentic content compounds。

Pick format can keep doing for couple of years。

Just keep showing up。

Video beats everything。

If had to pick one channel for someone starting today。

It's video。

YouTube，specifically。

Intent is higher，shelf life longer。

One good video can carry for years。

Written content great，short-form great。

But nothing has been as durable as long-form videos on YouTube。

The truth is，most of game just outlasting people who give up at month three。
